verdict.headline: BUY / ADD — FUNDAMENTALS AND TECHNICALS ARE ALIGNED
verdict.subhead: FUNDAMENTALS STRONG (all three parts score 1.0)   |   TECHNICALS BULLISH / UPTREND INTACT
verdict.summary: GILD scores a full 3.0/3.0. Gross margin has expanded every year since FY23 (77.99% to 79.60% ttm) off an already-high base, trailing free cash flow is a record $12.94B, and ROIC is 34.4%. Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% to $7.803B — the strongest second-quarter growth in three years — led by HIV at $5.693B (+12%), and management RAISED full-year HIV growth guidance to 9-10% from 8%. Technicals are bullish and aligned: price $151.22 sits above every major moving average (MA20 144.35 / MA50 136.60 / MA200 133.37) with RSI(14) at 67.7 and the Street's average target ABOVE the price. The catch is not the business — it is the GAAP optics. A $10.5B Q2 net loss and a negative trailing P/E are the product of $11.1B of acquired IPR&D expensed upfront on three acquisitions, plus a $1.75B impairment on assets from the earlier Immunomedics deal. Excluding those charges, management guides FY26 non-GAAP EPS of $8.50-$8.85, roughly 17x the current price.

assessment.heading: ASSESSMENT: NOT A DIVERGENCE BETWEEN PRICE AND FUNDAMENTALS — A DIVERGENCE BETWEEN ACCOUNTING AND CASH.
assessment.text: The usual actionable setups are strong-fundamentals/weak-tape or weak-fundamentals/euphoric-tape. GILD is neither: fundamentals and technicals agree. The exploitable gap here is mechanical. Screens that rank on GAAP earnings see a company with negative trailing EPS, a negative 20.7% ROE and no P/E, because $11.1B of acquisition cost was expensed in a single quarter rather than capitalised. The same company produced $3.43B of free cash flow in that quarter and $12.94B over the trailing year. Investors who read the GAAP line literally will misprice this; the risk is that the market is already awake to it, since the consensus target sits just 4.1% above the price.

catalyst.title: Long-Acting HIV Prevention — Is GILD the Right Horse?

blocks.heading: 1. Yeztugo is winning the PrEP switch market
bullets: Twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir booked $232M in Q2 2026 against $15M a year earlier, +40% sequentially, beating consensus by $17M (8%). Four full quarters after launch it leads the entire PrEP switch market and is the leading long-acting option for PrEP-naive patients.

blocks.heading: 2. The franchise is taking share, not riding a rising tide
bullets: Total PrEP sales topped $1B in a quarter for the first time ($1.03B), more than doubling YoY against a US PrEP market growing 14%. That gap is share capture. Annual run rate is now ~$4B.

blocks.heading: 3. Retention is holding so far
bullets: More than 70% of users returned for the six-month reinjection, extending protection to a full year. Management raised FY26 HIV growth guidance to 9-10% from 8% on the back of it.

blocks.heading: 4. HIV is the core, not a side bet
bullets: HIV is $5.693B of $7.803B total Q2 revenue — roughly 73%. Unlike a diversified beneficiary, GILD is a pure-play on the trend it is being bought for. Biktarvy alone is $3.772B (+7%).

right.title: THE CATCH (real, and worth sizing for)

blocks.heading: 1. GSK/ViiV has a tolerability edge
bullets: A head-to-head acceptability study found 4.4x more injection-site reaction events after Yeztugo than after GSK's Apretude, with 69% rating Apretude injections totally or very acceptable versus 48% for Yeztugo. Nine of ten participants preferred Apretude.

blocks.heading: 2. Analysts question durability
bullets: The 70% six-month persistence figure is encouraging but early; it is the single number that decides whether the $4B run rate compounds or plateaus. GSK's long-acting portfolio is also strong — LAIs are now 35% of its US HIV sales, with 77% of Cabenuva switches coming from competitors.

blocks.heading: 3. Oncology is the weak leg
bullets: Oncology grew just 3% to $873M, and the $1.75B impairment was taken against assets acquired from Immunomedics — the Trodelvy deal. That is a prior acquisition being written down while three more are being made.

blocks.heading: 4. Capital allocation is now the swing factor
bullets: $11.1B was committed upfront to Arcellx, Tubulis and Ouro Medicines. The operating business funds it comfortably, but the Immunomedics write-down is evidence that Gilead's deal record is not unblemished.

verdict.text: HIV VERDICT: GILD IS THE RIGHT HORSE. Unlike a peripheral beneficiary, Gilead sets the pace in the category it is valued for — 73% of revenue, the leading long-acting product, and share gains against a growing market. The honest caveats are Apretude's tolerability advantage, the unproven durability of Yeztugo persistence beyond the first year, and a demonstrated willingness to overpay for oncology assets.

parts.title: Part 1 — Quality Check (Margins & Profitability)
parts.question: Is the price move supported by margin trends?

rows.t: CLEARLY EXPANDING off a high base — 77.99% (FY23) to 78.26% (FY24) to 78.84% (FY25) to 79.60% (ttm). Q2 product gross margin 79.3% vs 78.7% a year earlier. Roughly +160bps over three years on an already best-in-class base.

STRONG — 34.40% (FY23) to 37.17% (FY24) to 40.13% (FY25), 38.88% ttm. The small step down from FY25 reflects higher R&D ($1.764B vs $1.491B) and SG&A ($1.921B vs $1.365B) behind the Yeztugo launch, not pricing erosion.
RECORD — trailing FCF $12.94B, up from $9.46B (FY25) and $7.42B (FY23). Q2 alone produced $3.432B against $720M a year earlier. Price/FCF 14.5x; ROIC 34.4%.

Trailing net income is -$3.24B, profit margin -10.64% and ROE -20.68%. This is entirely $11.1B of acquired IPR&D expensed upfront (Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro Medicines) plus the $1.75B Immunomedics impairment. It is capital deployment run through the income statement, not margin deterioration.
The $1.75B impairment is a write-down of assets from a PRIOR acquisition. Margin quality in the operating business is not in question; the discipline of the acquisition programme is.

Every operating measure of quality — gross margin, operating margin, free cash flow, ROIC — is strong and improving. The negative headline earnings are an artefact of accounting for acquisitions, and the market can see through it: the stock is 3.9% off its high, not distressed.

parts.title: Part 2 — Growth Check (Divisional & Franchise Momentum)
parts.question: Which division is driving growth? Is it sustainable?

rows.t: SECULAR / NEW-CATEGORY, not cyclical — the driver is a product cycle creating a new treatment category (twice-yearly injectable PrEP), not a restock or a price increase on legacy volume.
HIV — $5.693B, +12% YoY, ~73% of total revenue. Biktarvy $3.772B (+7%) is the stable base; Yeztugo is the growth vector at $232M from $15M a year ago, +40% sequentially.

RAISED — full-year HIV growth guidance lifted to 9-10% from a prior 8%; base business sales guided to $29.8-30.1B, up $350M at the midpoint versus May. Total Q2 growth of 10% was the strongest second quarter in three years.

rows: Liver Disease $877M (+10%) is a solid second leg. Veklury at $23M (-81%) is a COVID runoff now small enough to stop mattering, which removes a drag on FY27 comparisons.

rows.t: Oncology grew only 3% to $873M and carries the $1.75B Immunomedics impairment. Roughly 11% of revenue is not contributing to the growth case.

HIGH but not proven beyond year one — the whole thesis rests on Yeztugo persistence. The 70%+ six-month reinjection rate is the number to track each quarter; if it holds, growth compounds, if it decays, the $4B run rate plateaus.

boxes.title: Why this is a 1.0
bullets: GILD is a pure-play on the trend, not a diversified beneficiary — HIV is 73% of revenue.
It is demonstrably gaining share: PrEP sales doubled while the market grew 14%.
It sets the pace on dosing convenience, the axis patients switch for.

boxes.title: What would break it
bullets: Injection-site tolerability is a genuine, measured disadvantage versus Apretude.
If six-month persistence slips below ~70%, the leadership claim weakens fast.
GSK is not retreating — its long-acting franchise is growing and taking switches too.

finalVerdict.reasoning: All three parts score 1.0 and the technical overlay is bullish rather than euphoric — RSI 67.7 with price above every major moving average and the Street's average target still above the price. Per the rubric's matrix, high fundamentals plus aligned bullish technicals is a Buy/Add, and there is no falling-knife or take-profit divergence to arbitrage here. Two disciplines apply. First, the reward is modest against consensus: $157.41 is only 4.1% away, so the case for size rests on the $180 Street high and on FY26 earnings power of $8.50-$8.85 ex-charges, roughly 17x. Second, the stop must sit below $137.55 — verified support and the MA50 — because a stop placed just above it will be taken out on an ordinary test. Track one number: Yeztugo six-month persistence, currently above 70%. It is the hinge on which both the Growth and Peer scores turn.
